Metadata.Title: Dark Souls III
Metadata.Name: Double Sound Update Rate
Metadata.Note: The sound engine (FromSoftware's MagicOrchestra over FMOD) takes the game's sound orders, a sound started, stopped or moved, once every MainThreadUpdateTime microseconds of its setup text: 33333, 30 times a second, whatever the frame rate. This halves the number that is there, so the orders are taken twice as often: 60 times a second, and 120 where another patch (Bloodborne's 60 FPS++) has made it 60 already. A sound the game starts waits half as long to be taken up. Found by the text itself, so every version of the game that has the line gets it.

Metadata.Title: Dark Souls III
Metadata.Name: Lower Audio Latency
Metadata.Note: FMOD mixes the game's sound ahead of the speakers in blocks of 256 samples and keeps 4 of them: 1024 samples, 21 milliseconds, between a sound being mixed and being heard. This makes it keep 2, the fewest FMOD takes: 512 samples, 11 milliseconds. Blocks cannot be shorter than 256 samples, the console's smallest. If the sound crackles, the mixer is not keeping up with 2: turn this off. Found by FMOD's own code, so every version of the game that has it gets it.
